name: runc
description: Reference OCI Runtime CLI. Reads an OCI bundle (config.json + rootfs) and uses Linux primitives (namespaces, cgroups, capabilities, seccomp, AppArmor) to create and run a container. Default low-level runtime under containerd. Operations: create, start, run, exec, kill, delete, state, spec, list, ps, update, pause, resume, checkpoint, restore. Self-managing: each run leaves on-disk state under /run/runc/<id>/. Engine perspective in docker/engine; this leaf catalogs the OCI-runtime-spec contract it implements.

name: containerd
description: Container lifecycle daemon — process supervisor + content store + image store + snapshotter manager + grpc API. Sits between dockerd / kubelet and runc. Listens on `/run/containerd/containerd.sock`. State under /var/lib/containerd, runtime under /run/containerd. Plugin architecture: each major subsystem (snapshotter, runtime, content store, metadata, CRI) is a plugin; configurable via /etc/containerd/config.toml.

name: containerd-shim-runc-v2
description: Per-container shim binary that owns the container's pid 1 from containerd's perspective. Decouples container lifetime from containerd's: containerd can be restarted without killing every container (the shim continues holding the pid). Implements the containerd shim v2 API. Alternative shims (e.g. containerd-shim-kata-v2, containerd-shim-runsc-v1, containerd-shim-wasmtime-v1) are how runtimes other than runc plug in.

name: containerd CRI plugin
description: containerd's built-in implementation of the Kubernetes Container Runtime Interface (CRI). Lets kubelet talk to containerd directly via grpc on `/run/containerd/containerd.sock`. Configured under [plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri"] in containerd's config.toml. Owns sandbox-pause-image, default runtime selection, registry mirrors, image decryption, snapshotter choice. The reason `dockerd` is no longer needed for k8s nodes since k8s 1.24.

name: containerd snapshotter
description: containerd plugin that provides image-layer storage as snapshots. Built-in: overlayfs, native, btrfs, zfs, devmapper, fuse-overlayfs. Each snapshotter exposes prepare/view/commit/remove ops; lifetime is per-key under /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.<name>/. Default per-runtime snapshotter is configurable in CRI plugin. The runtime-leaf analogue of docker/engine's storage-driver concept.

name: containerd content store
description: Content-addressable blob store (`/var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.content.v1.content/blobs/<algorithm>/<digest>`). Holds image manifests, configs, and compressed layer tarballs keyed by digest. Garbage collection per labels; references from snapshotters / image store keep blobs alive.

name: containerd tasks service
description: grpc service inside containerd for managing running container processes ("tasks"). Distinguished from "containers" (configured but not running) — `ctr container ls` vs `ctr task ls`. Tasks have pids, exit codes, and metrics endpoints. Operations: create, start, kill, delete, exec, pause, resume, checkpoint, metrics.

name: containerd events service
description: grpc event stream for lifecycle events (image pull, container create/start/exit, snapshot prepare/commit, etc.). Consumers: dockerd, kubelet, observability sidecars. `ctr events` to tail the stream.

name: OCI runtime CLI contract
description: The general-operation contract every OCI-compliant runtime implements: create / start / kill / delete / state / exec. NOT a specific CLI surface — an abstract API. Each runtime exposes it via its own command line (runc, crun, youki, runsc); shims invoke runtimes through this contract. Defined in `oci-runtime-spec-runtime`.

name: OCI bundle
description: On-disk directory comprising a `config.json` (the OCI runtime config) plus a `rootfs/` directory (the container's filesystem). The unit `runc create <id> <bundle>` consumes. dockerd/containerd assemble it dynamically from the image; standalone runc usage does it by hand (`docker export | tar -x`, `runc spec`, edit, `runc run`).

name: OCI image manifest
description: `application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json` document describing one platform-specific image: schemaVersion=2, config descriptor (points to the image config blob), layers[] (descriptors of layer tarballs), optional subject (referrers chain), optional annotations. The thing pulled by digest from a registry; binds a config to its layer set.

name: OCI image config
description: `application/vnd.oci.image.config.v1+json` blob describing the runtime defaults of an image: created, author, architecture, os, os.version, os.features, variant, config{User, ExposedPorts, Env, Entrypoint, Cmd, Volumes, WorkingDir, Labels, StopSignal}, rootfs{type="layers", diff_ids[]}, history[]. Content of `docker inspect`'s Config block.

name: OCI image index
description: `application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json` — the multi-arch "fat manifest". Contains a manifests[] array of descriptors, each with a platform (os, architecture, variant). Registry returns this for a single tag like `nginx:1.27` so a pull can pick the right per-arch manifest. Equivalent to Docker's manifest-list-v2.

name: OCI content descriptor
description: The pointer used everywhere in OCI to reference content: {mediaType, digest, size, urls?, annotations?, data?, artifactType?}. Unique because it carries both the type and the cryptographic hash — content can be located + verified from any source. Used in manifests, indexes, the referrers API.

name: OCI image layout
description: Filesystem layout for a portable image directory: `oci-layout` file (version), `index.json` (top-level index with descriptors), `blobs/<algorithm>/<digest>` files. Produced by `docker save` (in OCI mode), consumable by `docker load` / `skopeo copy oci:dir`. The on-disk shape of an image archive.

name: Content blob
description: A single content-addressable file in the content store / image layout / registry. Three flavors as far as images are concerned: layer (compressed tarball), config (json), manifest/index (json). Identified by digest; size and media-type carried in the descriptor that points to it.

name: Image tag reference
description: Mutable named pointer (`<registry>/<repo>:<tag>` or `<repo>@<digest>`) at a registry. The bytes resolved by a tag can change over time; a digest reference is immutable. The referrers API extends this with a third form (subject-relations).

name: OCI media type
description: RFC-6838 MIME-style type carried by every descriptor. Compatibility matrix: `application/vnd.oci.image.{manifest,index,config,layer.v1.tar[+gzip|+zstd]}.v1+json` are OCI; Docker compat: `application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.{v1,v2}+json`, `application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.diff.tar.gzip`, etc. Unknown types MUST be passed through unchanged — the spec forbids erroring on unknown.

name: containerd task
description: A running container instance from containerd's POV. `ctr container create` makes a container record; `ctr task start <id>` materializes a Task that has a pid and OS-level resources. Task lifecycle is independent of the container record — you can delete the task and re-start it from the same container.

name: Layer tarball
description: The compressed tarball that materializes one image layer's filesystem changeset. Two media types in common use: `application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+gzip` and `application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+zstd` (newer, faster). The body is a tar of additions/changes/deletes (whiteout files for deletes) relative to the parent layer.

name: OCI process spec
description: `config.json` `process` block: terminal, user{uid,gid,additionalGids}, args, env, cwd, capabilities (bounding/effective/inheritable/permitted/ambient), rlimits, noNewPrivileges, apparmorProfile, selinuxLabel, oomScoreAdj. Override-able via `runc exec --process <process.json>` for one-off exec ins.

name: PID namespace (runtime view)
description: OCI runtime-spec namespace `type: pid`. Container processes only see their own pid tree; container's pid 1 is not host's pid 1. Joining another's via `path: /proc/<pid>/ns/pid`.

name: Mount namespace
description: OCI namespace `type: mount`. Isolated mount table — bind mounts/volumes are visible only inside.

name: Network namespace
description: OCI namespace `type: network`. Each ns has its own interfaces, routing, iptables rules. Detail of how Docker wires veths into bridges lives in docker/networking.

name: UTS namespace
description: OCI namespace `type: uts`. Hostname + domainname isolation. Set via `hostname`/`domainname` in config.json.

name: IPC namespace
description: OCI namespace `type: ipc`. SysV IPC and POSIX message-queue isolation.

name: User namespace
description: OCI namespace `type: user`. Container uid/gid → host uid/gid mapped via `uidMappings[]` / `gidMappings[]` (containerID, hostID, size triples). Foundation for rootless and userns-remap. Number of mapping entries kernel-limited.

name: Cgroup namespace
description: OCI namespace `type: cgroup`. Hides the host's cgroup tree; container sees only its own subtree at root. Required for cgroup-delegation in unprivileged contexts.

name: Time namespace
description: OCI namespace `type: time`. Container can have its own clocks; offsets per clock via `timeOffsets`. Newer kernel feature; not all runtimes implement.

name: Linux capability (runtime view)
description: Subdivision of root power applied per container: bounding, effective, inheritable, permitted, ambient sets. config.json's `process.capabilities` enumerates them. The runtime applies them via prctl + setuid sequencing.

name: cgroup controller
description: Kernel cgroup subsystem (cpu, memory, pids, blkio, freezer, devices, hugetlb, perf_event, net_cls, net_prio, rdma). Each enforces one resource axis. config.json's `linux.resources.<controller>.*` sets per-container limits. cgroup v1 = multiple hierarchies, one per controller; v2 = unified hierarchy.

name: runc state: creating
description: OCI runtime state during step 2 of the lifecycle — env being set up. `runc create` not yet returned. Brief; container has an ID but no pid yet.

name: runc state: created
description: After `runc create` returned but before `runc start`. Container's resources (namespaces, cgroups, mounts) are in place; the user-specified process has not been exec'd. `runc state` returns this until `start` fires.

name: runc state: running
description: After step 8 — user process has been exec'd and hasn't exited. `pid` field is set in the state JSON.

name: runc state: stopped
description: Container process has exited (cleanly, error, or via `runc kill`). Resources still on-disk until `runc delete`.

name: OCI container lifecycle
description: The 13-step lifecycle: create → prestart hooks → createRuntime hooks → createContainer hooks → start → startContainer hooks → exec user process → poststart hooks → process exits → delete → poststop hooks. Each numbered step in `oci-runtime-spec-runtime`. Hook failures jump to step 12 (destroy).

name: Exit status
description: `runc exec` exits with the user command's exit status (or 255 on internal error). Detail of conventional codes lives in docker/engine (137 = OOM, 139 = SEGV, 143 = SIGTERM, 128+N = signal-N termination).

name: overlayfs snapshotter
description: containerd snapshotter plugin `io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs`. Default on Linux. Backed by kernel OverlayFS (same primitive as the engine-side overlay2 storage driver). Per-snapshot dirs at /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/<id>/{fs,work}. Engine-perspective in docker/engine; this is the runtime-leaf view.

name: native snapshotter
description: `io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.native`. Like vfs — full file copy per layer. Used as a fallback when no other snapshotter is available.

name: btrfs snapshotter
description: `io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.btrfs`. Requires /var/lib/containerd on btrfs. Uses btrfs subvolumes/snapshots; block-level CoW.

name: zfs snapshotter
description: `io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.zfs`. Requires zfs filesystem. Block-level CoW; high RAM (ARC).

name: devmapper snapshotter
description: `io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.devmapper`. Uses LVM thin-pool. Per-container thin volume; configurable basesize. Legacy on most distros.

name: fuse-overlayfs snapshotter
description: FUSE-mode overlay for rootless containerd. Slower than kernel overlayfs but doesn't require CAP_SYS_ADMIN. Selected automatically in rootless mode where overlayfs needs kernel ≥ 5.11.

name: Docker manifest v2-2
description: `application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json`. Docker's pre-OCI manifest format; OCI image manifest v1 is binary-compatible. Most registries accept both; pulls succeed regardless. Specific compatibility quirks (history, fsLayers) are docker-v2-1-only.

name: Manifest list (multi-arch)
description: `application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json` — Docker's multi-arch wrapper. Each entry has a per-platform descriptor + platform={os, architecture, variant}. OCI equivalent is `image-index`. Modern registries return one or the other depending on Accept header.

name: OCI manifest
description: `application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json`. Same shape as docker v2-2 but media types under `vnd.oci.*`. Most registries accept both; OCI is the future-default.

name: Cross-repository blob mount
description: `POST /v2/<name>/blobs/uploads/?mount=<digest>&from=<other-repo>`. Lets a push reuse a blob already present in another repo on the same registry, without re-uploading. The reason `docker push` is fast for a layer-shared image to a different repo on the same registry.

name: Chunked blob upload
description: Multi-PATCH protocol for layer uploads. `POST /v2/<name>/blobs/uploads/` returns a `Location:` URL; client `PATCH`es with Content-Range; final `PUT ?digest=sha256:...` finalizes. Resumable; required for very large layers over flaky links.

name: Monolithic blob upload
description: Single-request blob upload: `POST /v2/<name>/blobs/uploads/?digest=sha256:<digest>` with body. Faster than chunked when bandwidth and the layer fit. Server may not support it; fall back to chunked.

name: Range request (registry pull)
description: `Range: bytes=START-END` on `GET /v2/<name>/blobs/<digest>` for partial blob retrieval. Used by tools that resume failed pulls or stream-decompress layers.

name: Registry bearer-token auth
description: OAuth2-style flow used by Docker Hub / GHCR / GCR. Client gets `401 Unauthorized` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm=...,service=...,scope=...`, fetches a token from the realm, retries with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The reason an `unauthorized: authentication required` shows mid-pull when a token expired.

name: WWW-Authenticate challenge
description: Header in a registry's 401 response telling the client where to fetch a token from and which scope to request. Standard format: `Bearer realm="https://auth.docker.io/token",service="registry.docker.io",scope="repository:library/nginx:pull"`.

name: Referrers API
description: `GET /v2/<name>/referrers/<digest>`. Returns an OCI image-index of manifests whose `subject` field references the supplied digest. Foundation for SBOM / signature attachment to images. Modern registries; fallback via `referrers` tag schema for older.

name: OCI distribution error codes
description: Standard error codes registries return: BLOB_UNKNOWN, BLOB_UPLOAD_INVALID, BLOB_UPLOAD_UNKNOWN, DIGEST_INVALID, MANIFEST_BLOB_UNKNOWN, MANIFEST_INVALID, MANIFEST_UNKNOWN, NAME_INVALID, NAME_UNKNOWN, SIZE_INVALID, UNAUTHORIZED, DENIED, UNSUPPORTED, TOOMANYREQUESTS. Returned in JSON `{errors: [{code, message, detail}]}` body of 4xx responses.

name: prestart hook
description: OCI hook (deprecated in newer spec but still supported by runc). Runs in the runtime namespace, after the container's namespaces are created but before pivot_root. Failure → runtime errors out, container destroyed. Used historically for `nvidia-container-runtime-hook`.

name: createRuntime hook
description: Replaces prestart for runtime-namespace work. Runs after container namespaces created, before pivot_root. Same execution context as prestart but properly named.

name: createContainer hook
description: Runs in the container namespace before pivot_root. Has access to the container's mounts at their pre-pivot paths (i.e. /rootfs/...). For modifying container fs before the user process sees it.

name: startContainer hook
description: Runs in the container namespace, after pivot_root, immediately before the user-specified program is exec'd. Last chance to set up environment from inside the container.

name: poststop hook
description: Runs after the container is destroyed (step 13). Failures only logged as warnings — lifecycle continues. Used for cleanup (release GPUs, release netns, etc.).

name: sha256 digest
description: `sha256:<64 hex chars>` — the registered OCI digest algorithm. Verifies content integrity end-to-end. Other registered algos: sha512, blake3. Implementations SHOULD pass through unrecognized algorithms if they comply with the digest grammar.

name: Content-addressable storage
description: Files keyed by hash of their content. Two pulls of the same digest = identical bytes. Foundation for layer dedup, registry caching, image signing. Also surfaced from docker/engine; here the runtime-leaf view (containerd content store, blob layout).

name: tar-split
description: Library for reproducibly serializing tar headers separately from file contents so a layer's diff_id is stable across compress/decompress cycles. Required to compute consistent diff_ids, which feed into ChainID, which feeds into ImageID.

name: ImageID
description: sha256 of the image config blob. Content-addressable identifier of a fully-realized image (config + ordered diff_ids). What `docker image ls` shows (truncated) under IMAGE ID. NOT the same as the layer digests in the manifest.

name: Layer DiffID
description: sha256 of the UNCOMPRESSED layer tarball. Stable across compression algorithms; sits in `image-config.rootfs.diff_ids[]`. Distinct from the layer descriptor's digest, which is over the on-wire compressed bytes.

name: Layer ChainID
description: Recursive sha256 over a stack of DiffIDs: ChainID(L₀)=DiffID(L₀); ChainID(L₀..Lₙ)=Digest(ChainID(L₀..Lₙ₋₁) + " " + DiffID(Lₙ)). The unambiguous identifier for an applied stack of layers (vs. a single layer's DiffID, which doesn't capture order).

name: Image config history
description: `history[]` array in the image config: per-layer {created, created_by (Dockerfile instruction), author?, comment?, empty_layer?}. Surfaced by `docker history <image>`. The ground truth for 'why is this layer 800MB'.

name: OCI platform
description: {architecture, os, os.version?, os.features?, variant?} tuple per platform-specific manifest. Must match GOOS/GOARCH values: amd64, arm64, arm/v7, arm/v6, ppc64le, s390x, riscv64, mips64le, etc. Platform mismatch = registry returns the closest manifest or errors.

name: Runtime platform spec
description: Platform-spec object in the OCI runtime spec (linux | windows | solaris | vm). Selects which top-level config block applies. Linux has the richest schema; runc only implements linux.

name: seccomp syscall action
description: What seccomp does on a matching syscall: SCMP_ACT_ALLOW, SCMP_ACT_ERRNO[(errno)], SCMP_ACT_KILL, SCMP_ACT_KILL_PROCESS, SCMP_ACT_LOG, SCMP_ACT_TRACE[(ret)], SCMP_ACT_NOTIFY, SCMP_ACT_RET. config.json's `linux.seccomp.defaultAction` + per-syscall `syscalls[].action`. Detailed schema in docker/security.

name: Signal + stop timeout
description: OCI runtime: `runc kill <id> <signal>` sends signal to pid 1; default SIGTERM. No grace-period concept at runc layer — that lives in containerd / dockerd. Image's StopSignal sets the default kill signal; daemon's stop-timeout sets the grace before SIGKILL.

name: Exit code 128+signum convention
description: POSIX shell convention: process killed by signal N exits with status 128+N. Hence 137=SIGKILL(9), 139=SIGSEGV(11), 143=SIGTERM(15), 130=SIGINT(2). The thing the harness uses to translate `docker inspect ExitCode` into 'OOM-killed' / 'segfaulted' / 'cleanly stopped'.

name: Linux OOM killer
description: Kernel's response to memory exhaustion in a memory cgroup. Picks a process by `oom_score`; sends SIGKILL. Container exits with `State.OOMKilled=true` and ExitCode 137. Tunable via cgroup `memory.oom.group` (kill all-or-none) and `oom_score_adj`.

name: Terminal / pty
description: `process.terminal: true` requests a pty pair. The runtime opens a pty master in the runtime namespace and exposes it via `--console-socket` (an AF_UNIX socket the caller listens on). The container side gets the pty slave as fd 0/1/2.

name: console-socket
description: AF_UNIX socket path passed to runc `--console-socket` to receive the pty master fd via SCM_RIGHTS. The piece of plumbing that makes `runc run -t` actually deliver an attached terminal to the caller. Detail in `docs/terminals.md` upstream.

name: OCI linux spec
description: The `linux` block of config.json — namespaces, uidMappings, gidMappings, devices, cgroupsPath, resources, intelRdt, seccomp, maskedPaths, readonlyPaths, mountLabel, rootfsPropagation, sysctl. THE block runc applies on Linux hosts.

name: maskedPaths / readonlyPaths
description: Container hardening: `linux.maskedPaths[]` bind-mounts /dev/null over each path (typical: /proc/kcore, /proc/keys, /proc/timer_list, /proc/scsi, /sys/firmware). `linux.readonlyPaths[]` remounts paths read-only (typical: /proc/asound, /proc/bus, /proc/fs, /proc/irq, /proc/sys, /proc/sysrq-trigger). The reason `cat /proc/kcore` inside a default container shows nothing.

name: subreaper
description: Linux PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER prctl: marks a process as the reaper of orphaned descendants in its subtree (similar to pid 1 but local). runc uses one to reap reparented processes; `runc run --no-subreaper` disables it.

name: pivot_root vs --no-pivot
description: Standard runc switches the rootfs via pivot_root(2) syscall. `--no-pivot` falls back to chroot+chdir for environments where pivot_root is unavailable (e.g. RAM-disk or some container-in-container setups). Officially noted as 'may be unsafe from the security standpoint'.
